content.text: Call Bridge (also known as Call Break in South Asia) is a 4-player trick-taking card game enormously popular in Nepal, India, and Bangladesh. It resembles Spades but with individual bidding â€” each player bids the number of tricks they will win, and Spades are permanent trump. Unlike exact-bid games, players must win AT LEAST their bid (over-tricks are allowed but under-tricks are penalised). It is one of the most widely played card games in Nepal.

Call Bridge/Call Break is deeply embedded in Nepali card culture and is widely played throughout South Asia. It likely developed from Whist-family games introduced during the British colonial period, merged with local bidding traditions.
52 standard cards. Spades are permanent trump.

items.text: Call Break (Nepal variant): Most common Nepali form. Identical mechanics. Often played to exactly 5 rounds.
